disagreements.positions: agent_1, agent_2 and agent_3 moved to an effective sigma of 44-46%, in line with the 47% trailing weekly realized volatility that round 1 found. agent_4 (~39%) and agent_5 (~41%) widened only part of the way. They argue that 12-month outcomes mean-revert, and agent_5 cites NXPI's own 12-month log-return dispersion of 0.29 (2011-2026) and 0.23 (2021-2026). The round-2 mean ladder implies ~43% around a ~$246 median.
disagreements.resolution: agent_5's figures are correct. I recomputed them from Twelve Data monthly closes: the standard deviation of 12-month log returns is 0.29 since 2011 and 0.23 since 2021, and monthly volatility annualizes to 37% over the long run. The current regime is much hotter, though: 52% on monthly closes over the last 12 months and 47% on weekly closes. A 12-month forecast should blend the two, with volatility mean-reverting from ~50% toward ~37% over the year. That gives ~40-42%, a little narrower than the mean. Historically, 12-month drops of 30% or more happened in only ~3% of windows since 2016, against ~18% in the mean ladder. That supports thinning the left tail slightly. I do not thin it back to history, because this is a late-cycle setup (channel build, serial price increases, a hiking Fed). I use an 85/15 lognormal mixture: sigma 0.38 at a $251 median, plus sigma 0.56 at a $225 median. The effective sigma is ~41%.
disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data NXPI monthly closes, Jan-2011 to Sep-2026 (own calculation): 12-month log-return s.d. 0.291 (177 windows), 0.269 since 2016 and 0.230 since 2021. Annualized monthly s.d. is 0.370 since 2011 and 0.526 over the last 12 months. Since 2016, 2.6% of 12-month windows fell 30% or more and 8.5% fell 25% or more.

disagreements.topic: Centre of the distribution: agent_3's cycle haircut
disagreements.positions: agent_3's median is ~$235 and its P(>=236) is 0.495. It haircuts the growth rate into 2028 by 8% (horizon NTM EPS $18.0 vs ~$19.5 rolled forward), citing late-cycle signs and sell-side cuts 'after Q2 (TD Cowen $290, UBS $270, Mizuho underperform)'. The other four put the median at ~$250-251 and P(>=236) at 0.55-0.56.
disagreements.resolution: The late-cycle signals are real, but the same facts (lead times of 40-52 weeks, a third round of price increases, channel inventory at 11 weeks against 9) are already priced into every agent's fatter left tail. Using them again to lower the median counts them twice. agent_3 misdates one of its three cited cuts: Mizuho's downgrade was on 2026-04-16, before Q2, not after. After the Q2 print only TD Cowen and UBS cut. On the other side, consensus 2027 EPS rose from $17.71 to $18.10 in 30 days. On Sep 9 management said pricing benefits build 'through the third quarter, fourth quarter and into next year' and that channel inventory is 'steady at 11 weeks'. I keep the centre at the group's ~$247-250 median (P(>=236) 0.55) and do not follow agent_3 lower.
disagreements.evidence: Seeking Alpha 2026-04-16 (Mizuho cut). Yahoo estimates (2027 EPS $17.71 to $18.10 in 30 days). NXP at Goldman Sachs Communacopia, 2026-09-09 (Investing.com transcript summary).

disagreements.topic: Sell-in risk: distribution vs direct revenue
disagreements.positions: New from agent_1 in round 2: distributor revenue grew +26.7% y/y against +9.4% for direct sales and is 59% of revenue, a larger pull-in exposure than China (18%). The others focus on China and channel weeks.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed in the 10-Q. Q2 2026 distributor revenue was $2,072M against $1,636M a year earlier (+26.7%). Direct revenue was $1,375M against $1,257M (+9.4%). Distributors were 59.3% of the $3,496M total, and distributor revenue grew +11% q/q ($1,862M in Q1). Channel inventory rose only from 9 to 11 weeks, so most of the distribution growth is sell-through rather than stocking. Management said on Sep 9 that channel inventory was steady at 11 weeks and that its forecasts assume no OEM restocking. This is the right thing to watch in the Oct 27 print (distributor weeks, disti versus direct growth). It is a left-tail risk and does not change the median.
disagreements.evidence: NXP 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-28, Note 5 revenue by sales channel. Goldman Sachs conference, 2026-09-09.

disagreements.positions: agent_4 reports a third NXP price round (~10%, notice dated Sep 2, effective Sep 28) and says September trackers show allocation still tightening, with auto MCU prices up 15-20% cumulatively. agent_2 and agent_3 cite the same Electronics Risk Brief Substack for lead times of 40-52 weeks.
disagreements.resolution: The Substack is a paid newsletter. It relays EE Times China and TrendForce reports on STMicro's third 2026 price increase (Aug 23), and its excerpt does not mention NXP. The '15-20% cumulative auto MCU' figure is about ST and the sector, not NXP. So agent_2 (TrendForce Aug 21 plus the Substack) and agent_4 counted one original twice. The NXP September round rests on a single distributor blog (Aetrix) that paraphrases a customer notice. My search found no second source (only the April and June rounds are corroborated, by TrendForce and distributor notices). It fits management's comment that pricing will build into 2027, but it should not move numbers. agent_4 already kept it out of base EPS, which is correct.
disagreements.evidence: electronicsriskbrief.substack.com, 2026-09-03. Aetrix blog, 2026-09. TrendForce 2026-03-12, 2026-05-11 and 2026-08-21. Microchip USA 2026-04-07 (April round only).

disagreements.positions: In round 1, agent_5 said hiking into an upcycle precedes analog tops. In round 2 it computes that analog semis rose in the 12 months after a first hike in 7 of 8 cases (median ~+16%). The others treat the Sep 16 hike only as a cap on the multiple.
disagreements.resolution: I verified the NXPI entries: Dec-2015 $84.25 to Dec-2016 $98.01 (+16%) and Mar-2022 $185.08 to Mar-2023 $186.48 (+1%). The sample is small (8 overlapping cases, 3 cycles), so it argues against a bearish median rather than for a bullish one. It is consistent with holding the multiple at ~14x rather than cutting it further, which is what all five now do.
disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data monthly closes (NXPI, own check). Federal Reserve implementation note, 2026-09-16.

disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data monthly lows: $183 in Nov 2025, $184.67 in Mar 2026.

one_month_reasoning: I keep the round-2 forecaster mean, since all five now agree to within about 1.5 points at spot. The window holds the Q3 print (Oct 27 after the close, first reaction Oct 28; guide $3.75B / $4.11) and the FOMC decision on Oct 28. TXN and STM report the week before. The last two earnings weeks moved +21% and -15%, so the event gap is two-sided.
confidence_reason: The five forecasts converged in round 2: P(>=spot) ranges from 0.495 to 0.559 and fair values from $253 to $271. What remains is mostly the width of the distribution. I verified the base-rate data behind the narrower view (12-month log-return s.d. of 0.23-0.29 against 47-52% current realized volatility). That supports a small narrowing, mainly in the left tail, but it is a forecast of volatility, not a settled fact. My changes are therefore small (at most 0.02 per strike), and I do not claim high confidence.
thesis_break_reason: $175 is below the $183 52-week low and ~9.7x the $18.10 2027 consensus EPS. A close there would mean the market is pricing an earnings reset: distributor sell-in unwinding (distribution +26.7% y/y against +9.4% direct, channel inventory 11 weeks against 9), China correcting (+25.5% y/y against car retail -20.8% YTD), pricing reversing, or a rate-driven downturn. Moves in the $200-230 range are ordinary for this stock. Confirm the break on a close, not an intraday print.
key_drivers: Fundamentals are still accelerating: Q2 revenue was $3.50B (+19.5% y/y) and the Q3 guide is $3.75B / $4.11 EPS. 2027 consensus EPS of $18.10 is rising ($17.71 a month ago), so the stock trades at ~13x.

Sell-in is the main risk, not China alone. Distributor revenue grew +26.7% y/y against +9.4% for direct sales and is 59% of revenue (10-Q), and channel inventory is 11 weeks against 9. Watch both in the Oct 27 print.

Pricing power is sector-wide (ST's third 2026 increase, TI, Infineon; lead times of 40-52 weeks), and NXP says its pricing builds into 2027. A third NXP round in September is reported by only one source.

Rates cap the multiple: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 and meets on Oct 28. All five agents now use ~14x. After past first hikes, analog semis still rose over the next 12 months in 7 of 8 cases.
Volatility is high but mean-reverting: realized is 47-52% now, while 12-month dispersion has historically been 0.23-0.29, so an effective ~41% is the reconciled width.

fair_value.reason: 60% weight on 14x a ~$19.2 NTM EPS at Sep-2027 (2027 consensus $18.10 rolled forward with a small cycle haircut) = ~$269, and 40% on ~$15 of 2027 FCF per share (24% margin on ~$15.9B revenue, ~252M shares) at a 6% yield = ~$250. Blended, ~$262. This equals the round-2 agent mean ($262.2). No agent's inputs needed correcting this round: share count, EPS base, net debt and multiples are now consistent across all five. It is down from my round-1 $265 because four of five agents tightened multiples and yields for the Sep 16 hike.

summary: Round 2 converged: all five now use ~14x a ~$19 NTM EPS because of the Sep 16 Fed hike, fair values sit at $253-271 (mean $262), and P(close >= $236) is 0.50-0.56. My fact-checks confirmed agent_1's new sell-in flag (distributor revenue +26.7% y/y against +9.4% direct, 59% of sales, 10-Q). They found the NXP September price round is single-sourced and the sector-pricing figures are ST data relayed by a Substack. They also confirmed agent_5's base rates: analog semis rose in 12 months after a first hike in 7 of 8 cases, and NXPI's 12-month dispersion is 0.23-0.29. I keep the median near $247-250 and fair value at $262, and narrow the distribution slightly to ~41% effective sigma, mostly in the left tail. The Oct 27 print (watch distributor weeks) and the Oct 28 FOMC are the near-term binaries.
